transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 46 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Perez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Emberline, Head of ML), Daniel Cho (Platform Eng), Rhea Kapoor (Procurement), Leo Park (SRE)

Summary: quick renewal/scale check; Emberline looking to increase baseline capacity, add EU region (Frankfurt) and a smaller APAC edge (Tokyo), evaluate contract term extension and pricing; security and private deployment gating items discussed; agreed to run an EU latency/cost benchmark and deliver pricing options.

Topics: renewal timing, baseline v burst capacity, regional provisioning, private/VPC deployment questions, SOC2/KMS, procurement timeline, benchmark plan

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jordan Perez: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time today. quick check-in ahead of your renewal; wanted to run through capacity needs and the multi-region ask.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: Yeah thanks Jordan, and uh hi Priya, Marcus. So, we've been running in us-west primarily, and the trial in us-east did fine but we've seen latencies from our EU customers spike. We're trying to avoid a big brownout when traffic shifts.
[00:33] Priya Shah: Totally, Sofia. Can you remind me of the 95th p95 you're seeing now for inference calls and the token profile? Is it chat-weighted or short prompts?
[00:46] Sofia Martinez: Mostly chat, avg sequence around 220 tokens but with a long tail. p95 sits around 380ms for us-west but jumps to 780ms from Frankfurt. That is unacceptable for product.
[01:05] Marcus Li: Ok that jump suggests cross-region egress and routing. Two paths here: provision a dedicated footprint in eu-central, or use regional routing to edge and failover to us-west. The former reduces latency but increases baseline commit.
[01:25] Daniel Cho: What's the delta on cost if we add a Frankfurt pool at our current commit? Rough numbers are fine, we just need to understand unit economics.
[01:36] Jordan Perez: For a rough estimate — adding a dedicated small pool (2x A100-equivalent) would bump monthly committed cost by about 45% vs current baseline. But per-token unit cost drops with local serving because you avoid egress and cross-region routing inefficiencies. We'll put concrete numbers in the pro forma.
[01:58] Rhea Kapoor: From procurement side I need to understand term options. Emberline prefers 24 months for better pricing but legal will need the usual indemnities and data residency clauses. Do you support EU data residency for logs and metrics?
[02:14] Priya Shah: Yes, we support regionally isolated telemetry for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we can set retention policies and region pinning; for Private/VPC we can keep logs inside the customer's VPC or on-prem. We'll share the audit playbook.
[02:36] Leo Park: Quick infra question — what does the connectivity look like for private? Is it an IPsec tunnel, direct connect, or SAML? We run strict egress rules.
[02:47] Marcus Li: We usually do an IPsec tunnel or direct connect depending on customer preference; certificate-based mTLS between agents. Also KMS integration is supported for model payload encryption. Note: on the transcript there may be a small mislabel — K V cache sometimes referenced — but we mean KV cache.
[03:09] Sofia Martinez: On the commit size — we want to avoid being locked into too big a baseline if traffic is spiky. Can we have a hybrid commit: smaller baseline in EU + burst lanes?
[03:20] Jordan Perez: Absolutely, we often structure deals with a firm baseline and a burst bucket that you pay at a reduced overage rate compared to pure on-demand. That keeps the visible unit economics friendly while handling spikes.
[03:36] Daniel Cho: For the benchmark, we want to run our real payload — are you alright with us sanitizing prod logs and sending a snippet? Also, how many tokens can you simulate in the test harness?
[03:49] Priya Shah: Yep, sanitized samples are perfect. Our benchmark harness can simulate up to 10k concurrent sessions in a dedicated pool; we'll align on the exact scenario. We recommend a few runs to measure cold vs warm KV-cache behavior.
[04:06] Jordan Perez: Next, procurement. Rhea, do you have a target for when you want the PO in place?
[04:13] Rhea Kapoor: Ideally before end of March. Legal needs 2–3 weeks once we submit the vendor docs. So getting pro forma pricing and SOC2 by mid-Feb makes that feasible.
[04:24] Marcus Li: We'll send SOC 2 Type II artifacts and a redacted architecture diagram. For KMS we list supported providers: AWS KMS, Google KMS, HashiCorp Vault — we can also do HSM via partner integrations.
[04:39] Sofia Martinez: Can you also share telemetry retention options? We need logs for 13 months for audits.
[04:45] Priya Shah: Yes — that's within our enterprise add-on. We can extend retention and provide an S3-compatible export. We'll add that to the checklist.
[04:55] [brief crosstalk] Daniel Cho: When you say dedicated small pool, is that gpus or virtual nodes? what's the underlying hardware?
[05:04] Jordan Perez: Good question — it's GPU-backed. We map to A100/H100-equivalent stacks depending on model and sequence length. We'll show the mapping so you can correlate to your latency targets.
[05:17] Sofia Martinez: Another ask — we have customers in APAC but traffic is lower; would a smaller Tokyo edge be possible for burst only?
[05:27] Marcus Li: Yes, we can provision an edge pool with autoscale and a very small baseline; it's useful to reduce cold-starts while keeping cost controlled.
[05:36] Rhea Kapoor: Are there any vendor lock-in implications for the KV cache or model weights? I need to present this to our CTO.
[05:45] Priya Shah: No lock-in to your app data; KV cache is ephemeral and doesn't contain PII unless you forward it. For models, if you choose to host privately, you control the model files. For hosted, model versions are managed but we provide export and pinned snapshots upon request in enterprise agreements.
[06:04] Sofia Martinez: About security reviews, can you do a closed door technical deep dive with our security team? They want to see network diagrams and the threat model.
[06:15] Jordan Perez: Yes, Marcus can lead that. We'll plan a 60–90 minute technical session focused on private deployment and SOC2 controls.
[06:24] [00:06:24] Rhea Kapoor: Will you accept a redline to the terms around data residency and audit rights?
[06:31] Jordan Perez: We'll review, but typical enterprise legal redlines are scoped. We can fast-track a legal review once we have an intent/commit level.
[06:40] Sofia Martinez: Ok let's talk numbers quick — if we commit to a 12-month baseline with the EU small pool and APAC edge burst, what's the ballpark monthly commitment?
[06:52] Jordan Perez: Very rough: if your current baseline is X, adding EU small pool moves committed spend to ~1.5X, adding APAC burst adds another ~0.15X. For 24-month terms we can drop unit price by 12–16% depending on tier. We'll put detailed tiers in the pro forma.
[07:11] Daniel Cho: And how fast can you provision the EU pool? We're hoping for a March 21 go-live if contract ready.
[07:19] Marcus Li: Provisioning of dedicated footprint typically takes 10–14 business days after we have network details and commitment. So March 21 is tight but possible if paperwork and network prep start this week.
[07:33] Sofia Martinez: That's good to know. We'll aim to decide term by Feb 21 then.
[07:39] Jordan Perez: Action items recap: Jordan will send pricing and term options; Priya will set up the benchmark and coordinate prompts; Marcus will send security pack and deployment checklist; Sofia will send workload sample; Rhea will start procurement intake.
[07:55] Rhea Kapoor: One more procurement nuance — our finance prefers quarterly invoicing for multi-region spend, is that something you can support?
[08:05] Jordan Perez: Yes, we can do quarterly invoices or monthly invoicing consolidated by region; we'll include invoicing frequency options in the pro forma.
[08:14] Sofia Martinez: Are there any downsides to going 24 months besides commitment? like slower flexibility on model upgrades?
[08:22] Priya Shah: Generally model upgrades are orthogonal; you can pin to versions and upgrade per-service. The main trade-off is commit size vs agility. For customers that expect rapid changes in footprint we recommend a shorter baseline + higher burst.
[08:37] Daniel Cho: Competitor question — we've had a brief conversation with VectorScale, they pitch spot pools and preemptible savings. How does Redwood compare?
[08:47] Jordan Perez: VectorScale focuses on spot infrastructure; Redwood emphasizes predictable latency and smart routing, plus enterprise features like private deployment and telemetry control. We can incorporate preemptible capacity for cost savings but treat it as non-SLA capacity.
[09:05] [pause] Sofia Martinez: ok this was helpful. I think we have a path to decision.
[09:11] Jordan Perez: Great — we will circulate the pro forma and SOC2 artifacts mid-week and get the benchmark scheduled. Any final questions?
[09:20] Leo Park: Can you include network ACL examples so we can pre-authorize IPs?
[09:25] Marcus Li: Yes — we'll include sample security groups, CIDR ranges, and port lists.
[09:30] Rhea Kapoor: Expect a procurement intake note from me by Friday.
[09:34] Jordan Perez: Perfect. Thanks everybody — we'll follow up with notes and deliverables.

End of call.
